free_tier.stated: no service and no account; source and pre-built static binaries

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: tcp

tooling: static binaries for x86, ARM, Android and some OpenWrt routers
chaining: only composes with a host a user rents or gets free, such as a free-tier VM, and adds nothing to a hosted tunnel.
binding_note: the constraint is a root Linux host with raw socket access at both ends, outside the seven-kind vocabulary

identity_cost.detail: no account; both ends are hosts the operator controls

reliability_note: needs root and iptables rules (-a), which is a common silent failure; the README states it survives reconnects and keeps UDP conversations valid
confidence_note: a measured run through a named path would raise it; no throughput number is published

evidence.proved: "turns UDP Traffic into Encrypted FakeTCP/UDP/ICMP Traffic by using Raw Socket" and "Linux host ... with root access"
the two-sided invocation: server '-s -l0.0.0.0:4096 -r 127.0.0.1:7777 --raw-mode faketcp' and client '-c -l0.0.0.0:3333 -r44.55.66.77:4096'
WireGuard names udp2raw as one of the projects that can transform its UDP packets into TCP

notes: WireGuard's own limitations page names this project, which is why it stays despite a 2023 release. It forges IP and TCP headers, so it cannot ride a CDN or any managed forwarder: the far end must be a host that accepts the forged connection. That is the opposite of the wstunnel case.

extras.wg_detail: "A Tunnel which turns UDP Traffic into Encrypted FakeTCP/UDP/ICMP Traffic by using Raw Socket"; WireGuard rides inside it because WireGuard is the UDP traffic
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: the bytes cross both hosts, with the far host forwarding to the WireGuard listener
extras.hosting_requirement: two root Linux hosts, one of them publicly reachable; fake-TCP needs raw sockets at both ends and cannot pass a managed HTTP forwarder
